halal_rules.problem: This food contains pork or pork-derived ingredients. Not suitable for halal diet.
action: Do not eat this food.
Find halal restaurants: HalalKorea.com or search 할랄 on Naver Maps
Ask: 할랄 음식 있나요? (do you have halal food?)
Itaewon area in Seoul has the most halal options

halal_rules.problem: This dish may contain alcohol as a cooking ingredient. Common in Korean marinades.
action: Ask: 이 음식에 술이 들어가나요? (Does this have alcohol?)
Choose steamed or boiled dishes — less likely to contain alcohol
Check packaging for 주정 (alcohol ingredient)

halal_rules.problem: This soup is made with PORK BONE broth. Even if you remove the meat, the broth itself contains pork.
action: Do not order this — the entire broth is pork-based
Safe alternatives: 미역국 (seaweed soup), 콩나물국 (bean sprout soup)
Look for restaurants with 소고기 국물 (beef broth) option

halal_rules.problem: Many Korean jellies, candies, and marshmallows contain GELATIN (젤라틴) derived from pig skin/bones. Not halal or vegetarian.
action: Avoid typical jellies (like Haribo, unless marked halal) and marshmallows.
Check ingredients for 식물성 젤라틴 (vegetable pectin/agar) as a safe alternative.
Traditional Korean sweets like 떡 (rice cakes) are gelatin-free and safe!

halal_rules.problem: Processed breads, pastries, and ramen may use SHORTENING (쇼트닝) or EMULSIFIERS (유화제) derived from animal fats (including lard/pork).
action: Check label for 식물성 유지 (vegetable fat) or 대두 (soy lecithin) which are safe.
If it only says '쇼트닝' or '유화제' without origin, it is doubtful (Mashbooh).
Halal-certified products in Asian marts are completely safe.

halal_rules.problem: Most Korean instant ramyeon (like Shin Ramyun) uses a beef-bone (사골) or pork-bone (돈골) based soup powder, even if it looks like just spicy powder.
action: Avoid standard ramyeon if halal/vegan
Look for 'Halal' certified Shin Ramyun at Itaewon or foreign marts
For vegans, buy '순라면' (Soon Veggie Noodle) or '정면' (Jeongmyeon)

halal_rules.problem: Even seemingly safe fast food options often cross-contaminate. Bulgogi sauce may contain cooking wine (mirin) and pork extract.
action: Fast food chains in Korea are generally not halal-certified
Burger buns may contain animal-derived shortening/emulsifiers
Avoid if strictly halal/vegan

vegan_rules.problem: This dish appears vegetarian but typically uses anchovy stock (멸치 육수) or fish sauce. Not vegetarian.
action: Ask: 멸치 육수 사용하나요? (Do you use anchovy broth?)
Request: 채소 육수로 만들어 주세요 (Please make with vegetable broth)
Temple food restaurants (사찰음식) serve strictly vegan Korean meals

vegan_rules.problem: This dish contains eggs (계란) or dairy (유제품), which are not vegan.
action: Avoid if strictly vegan
Ask: 계란 빼주세요 (Please remove eggs) or 치즈 빼주세요 (Please remove cheese)
Check ingredient labels for 우유 (milk) or 난류 (eggs)

vegan_rules.problem: Traditional Korean Kimchi almost always contains fish sauce (액젓) or fermented shrimp paste (새우젓). Not vegan/vegetarian.
action: Do not assume Kimchi is vegan
Ask: 이 김치에 젓갈 들어가나요? (Does this Kimchi have fish sauce?)
At convenience stores, only buy Kimchi explicitly marked '비건' (Vegan)

vegan_rules.problem: Gochujang and Ssamjang are generally vegan, but some cheap commercial brands might use trace amounts of beef extract (쇠고기 엑기스).
action: Generally safe for vegetarians, but strict vegans should check the label
Look for 쇠고기 (beef) on the back of the packet

vegan_rules.problem: Korean bakeries frequently use milk (우유), butter (버터), and eggs (계란) in almost all breads, including simple white bread.
action: Not suitable for strict vegans unless from a specific '비건 베이커리' (Vegan Bakery)
Ask: 우유나 계란 들어가나요? (Does it contain milk or eggs?)

vegan_rules.problem: Tteokbokki sauce is often made with anchovy broth (멸치 육수), and it always contains fish cakes (어묵). Not vegan or vegetarian.
action: Vegans should not eat street Tteokbokki
Ask: 어묵 빼주시고 물로 육수 내주실 수 있나요? (Can you remove fish cake and use water broth?) - though rarely possible for street food

general_rules.problem: Korean date formats are different. Make sure you understand which date is which.
action: 유통기한 = best before / sell-by (sometimes still edible after)
소비기한 = use-by / expiry (do NOT eat after this one)
제조일 = date it was made
Format is YYYY.MM.DD

general_rules.problem: Korean spicy food is MUCH hotter than you expect. Even 'mild' versions can be intense.
action: Start with 순한 맛 (mild flavor) option
Drink milk or eat rice to neutralize spice — NOT water
Say 덜 맵게 해주세요 (please make it less spicy)
